_comment: Vendored quote corpora — the re-import source of truth. The rows below are
the ONLY files `make import-quotes` reads; adding a language is one entry
here plus its upstream JSON beside this file.
`lang` is OUR language id — the same id the dictionary catalogue uses, so a
quote and a seeded run in the same language agree on what that language is
called. Upstream names its files differently for several of them, which is
why this mapping exists rather than a directory listing.
`groups` is NOT global: each corpus carries its own short/medium/long/thicc
thresholds, and chinese_simplified genuinely differs from the rest. The
importer MUST read each file's own `groups` array to assign len_group.
Recording them here too lets a test assert the vendored copy still matches
upstream instead of trusting a constant.

languages.why: served dictionary (arabian); upstream calls it arabic
served dictionary (chinese); upstream calls it chinese_simplified. NOTE the thresholds differ from every other corpus.
served dictionary (css_code); upstream calls it code_css
no seeded dictionary — quote-only language, added explicitly
no seeded dictionary — quote-only language, added explicitly

excluded.why: served dictionary, but upstream publishes no japanese quote corpus
served dictionary, but upstream publishes no chinese_traditional corpus
served dictionary (pre-reform orthography); no upstream counterpart
